articles.title: Phillies 2026 Offseason Guide on Free Agents, Trade Targets, Roster Shakeups After Wild Card Loss
articles.summary: For the fifth consecutive year, the Philadelphia Phillies reached the postseason. However, 2026, like the four prior years, saw them come up short of their final goal of winning the World Series.
articles.body:
For the fifth consecutive year, the Philadelphia Phillies reached the postseason. However, 2026, like the four prior years, saw them come up short of their final goal of winning the World Series.

This time, it was a 2-1 series loss to the rival Atlanta Braves in the wild card round.

Where will president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski—who has an uncomfortable number of players in or approaching their mid-30s—turn this offseason to get this group over the top while keeping the future in mind?

Here's the 2026 Phillies offseason guide.

Arraez narrowly missed becoming a four-time batting champion, although that has more to do with what he did in San Francisco than in Philadelphia. Arraez missed the wild card series after spraining his ankle just a few days before the postseason began.

Arraez's presence in the lineup behind Bryce Harper definitely had a positive effect. But whether it's because Bryson Stott goes back to second, Trea Turner moves there, or the Phillies are hesitant to make a long-term bet on Arraez defensively at the position, it's fair to wonder how likely he is to return.

Bohm finished runner-up in NL Rookie of the Year voting in 2020 and was the starting third baseman for the NL All-Star team in 2024. Still, many will view his tenure in Philadelphia as disappointing, given the belief that the former No. 3 overall pick could develop into a lineup anchor. He does hit well with runners in scoring position, so there will be interest in him on a one-year deal heading into his age-30 season. That interest probably won't be from the Phillies, however.

Since the Phillies acquired him from the St. Louis Cardinals before the 2022 trade deadline, Edmundo Sosa has become arguably the best utility man the Phillies have ever had. In addition to being able to play shortstop, second base and third base, Sosa proved capable of playing left field this season as well. The Phillies will likely want the 30-year-old back. It's just a matter of whether he gets an opportunity to play every day somewhere else.

The Phillies picked up José Alvarado's $9 million option for 2026 hoping he would be a dominant set-up man for Jhoan Duran. That's not what transpired, even if he was much better after posting a 6.82 ERA in 39 games in the first half of the season. The 31-year-old lefty was Dombrowski's first acquisition upon getting the job, and is well-liked by just about anyone he interacts with. Still, it feels like it might be time after six seasons with the Phillies.

The Phillies signed Adolis García to a one-year, $10 million deal, hoping he could bounce back after two consecutive poor seasons and finish his time with the Texas Rangers. Unfortunately, García tore his right lat in June, which required season-ending surgery. Before the injury, he had four outs above average in right field but was hitting just .195 with a .599 OPS. It's unclear what the market will look like for the former ALCS MVP ahead of his age-34 campaign.

Tim Mayza made the Phillies out of Spring Training as a non-roster invitee and proved to be arguably their best left-handed reliever in 2026. He'll turn 35 in January, but should have no problem securing an MLB deal this offseason.

Brooks Raley struggled mightily after being acquired by the Phillies at the trade deadline. However, he posted a 1.96 ERA in 45 games for the New York Mets before being dealt, so even heading into his age-39 season, Raley will have suitors.

First and foremost, Dombrowski needs to decide who the manager is.

The Phillies turned their 2026 campaign around under interim manager Mattingly, but only after Dombrowski tried to hire Alex Cora. By all accounts , Dombrowski will likely circle back and land Cora—who he won a World Series with in 2018—as his skipper for 2027.

Elsewhere, the Phillies need to decide on their infield makeup. Harper is almost certainly returning to first base. Bohm will likely walk in free agency. But will Arraez be back? Does Stott go back to second, stay at third or return to his natural position of shortstop? Is this the offseason the Phillies finally wave the white flag on Turner at shortstop? What, if anything, can be expected of top prospect Aidan Miller—a possible fit at shortstop or third base—after a back injury forced him to miss most of 2027?

Ultimately, Turner will play the biggest role in determining what the Phillies need. Right now, corner outfield seems like a major need. But if the Phillies try Turner in left field, then an infielder becomes more likely. Even if Turner stays in the infield, the Phillies likely will need a stopgap option until Miller is ready.

Additionally, the bullpen outside Duran—who will enter his final arbitration year in 2027—needs rebuilding.

Let's say the Phillies keep Turner in the infield, be it at shortstop or second base. That would mean they are short a corner outfielder if we assume Harper moves back to first base and Justin Crawford sticks in center field.

This isn't a great free-agent class, but both Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki will hit the market after career years and could be enticing to a Phillies team that's sought a right-handed bat for years on end. However, both will enter their age-32 seasons and have qualifying offers attached. So it's unclear if the Phillies will have the stomach to give either, let's say, five years.

Alternatively, Ian Happ could be worth watching. The switch-hitter is a four-time Gold Glove Award winner with six seasons of at least 20 homers on his resume. If the Chicago Cubs don't retain Happ, he could be an interesting target for the Phillies on a three-year deal ahead of his age-32 campaign.

ESPN's Jeff Passan linked the Phillies to Los Angeles Angels shortstop Zach Neto prior to the trade deadline. Ultimately, the Halos chose to keep him. Between an ownership change and uncertainty about John Mozeliak's future, it's unclear whether the Angels will be open to moving Neto in the offseason.

However, if the Phillies do move Turner off shortstop, their interest in Neto this past summer is worth remembering. He has three consecutive seasons of at least 23 homers and would give the Phillies another right-handed bat. Plus, for an aging team, adding a player before his age-26 season who can't become a free agent until after 2029 would be a boon.

The question is how turned off the Phillies would be by Neto's 200-plus strikeouts in 2026. Also, the top two defensive metrics—defensive runs saved and outs above average—differ greatly in how they view his work at shortstop. The last thing the Phillies want to do is move Turner off of shortstop and then acquire another player who doesn't fit there.

Neto will likely be a polarizing trade candidate because of the reasons outlined above. But it isn't hard to imagine Dombrowski becoming infatuated with the former first-round pick.

We predict the Phillies will cite Turner's defensive improvement over the final two months of the season as a reason to keep him at shortstop for at least another season. Stott would then shift back to second base, with Harper returning to first base. Aidan Miller looms over all of this, but it feels unlikely he'll be on the Opening Day roster. So the Phillies re-sign Sosa to be their third baseman until Miller is ready to take over.

There have been times during Crawford's rookie season when he's been an adventure in center field. But from a long-term sense, he's much more valuable in center field than left field. So the Crawford-Hill platoon will live to see another season, while Marsh, in his contract year, shifts to right to accommodate the free-agent signing of the aforementioned Happ.

With Nola's second-half resurgence and signs of growth from Painter, this might be baseball's best starting rotation entering 2027. Wheeler has long said he plans to retire after the 2027 season, when his contract concludes, although there seems to be some wiggle room on that.

articles.title: Braves hit 3 homers, including 3-run shot by Harris, to beat Phillies 6-2 in wild card clincher
articles.summary: Michael Harris II hit a three-run homer in the first inning, Ray Kerr threw 3 1/3 scoreless innings and the Atlanta Braves beat the Philadelphia Phillies 6-2 on Thursday night in the decisive Game 3 of their National League Wild Card Series.
articles.body: Michael Harris II hit a three-run homer in the first inning, Ray Kerr threw 3 1/3 scoreless innings and the Atlanta Braves beat the Philadelphia Phillies 6-2 on Thursday night in the decisive Game 3 of their National League Wild Card Series. Ozzie Albies launched a two-run homer in the fourth and Matt Olson added a solo shot in the seventh for the Braves, who advanced to a best-of-five Division Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers. The Braves took a postseason series for the first time since winning the 2021 World Series and earned their first playoff series win against the Phillies. Philadelphia beat Atlanta in the 1993 NL Championship Series and the 2022 and 2023 NLDS. After winning the NL East by six games over Philadelphia this year, the Braves came out on top in their postseason matchup, too. “Those guys kind of went start to finish in this division,” Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly said. “Over the course of the 162 (games), they were the best team in our division.” Phillies right-hander Aaron Nola was pulled after allowing three runs in 1 2/3 innings. Nola walked Ronald Acuña Jr. and Matt Olson with one out in the first before giving up the homer to Harris, who hit into two double plays in Wednesday’s 4-3 loss in 10 innings which forced Thursday night’s game. Kerr made his postseason debut in only fourth career start. Braves manager Walt Weiss wanted a left-hander to face Phillies left-handed hitters Kyle Schwarber and Bryce Harper at least once. Kerr allowed only one hit — to Schwarber in the first — and one walk - to Schwarber in the fourth. Right-hander Grant Holmes followed Kerr and allowed one run in two innings to earn the win. Kerr left to a standing ovation from the sellout crowd and acknowledged the cheers by lifting up his arm as he approached the dugout. Left-hander Chris Sale, the starter in Atlanta’s 5-3 win in Tuesday’s series opener, struck out Harper to end the eighth and closed out the win in the ninth by striking out Bryan De La Cruz and pinch-hitter Otto Kemp. Phillies right-hander Zack Wheeler, the winning pitcher in Sunday’s 7-3 victory over Tampa Bay that clinched the wild-card spot, walked Austin Riley in the fourth before giving up Albies’ homer to right field that gave Atlanta a 5-0 lead. Wheeler allowed two runs in four innings. Jonathan Bowlan, Philadelphia’s fourth pitcher, gave up Olson’s homer to center field. Kerr, 32, flourished in the postseason spotlight. He pitched in only nine games after being recalled by Atlanta on Aug. 16. He underwent Tommy John surgery in 2024 and didn’t pitch in 2025. Philadelphia’s 2022 World Series loss to Houston began a streak of five straight postseason appearances with progressively quicker exits — the NL Championship Series, two NLDS exits and now the wild-card loss. “If you don’t win the last game, it’s a crash landing no matter what. It doesn’t matter where it is,” Mattingly said. Night game brings quick sellout The game drew a sellout of 41,731 after the Braves fell short of sellouts in the first two games of the series, with school and work conflicting with the 2:15 p.m. first pitch for many fans. Afternoon starts also hurt attendance in other Wild Card Series games this week. The announced attendance at Truist Park was 30,127 on Tuesday and 37,150 on Wednesday. Injury update Edmundo Sosa remained in the Phillies’ starting lineup at third base after he appeared to aggravate a groin injury running to first base and left Wednesday’s game in the ninth inning. Mattingly said second baseman Luis Arraez, who was left off the roster for the series due to a left ankle sprain, has progressed to working in the weight room. Weiss said Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, who allowed only one run in seven innings on Wednesday despite feeling an abdominal pull in pregame warmups, was “feeling pretty good” on Thursday. Up next The Braves will play at Dodger Stadium on Saturday in the opening game of the Division Series.

articles.summary: Michael Harris II's three-run homer sparked the Atlanta Braves to a game three win over the Philadelphia Phillies at Truist Park on Thursday.
articles.body: While the three other wild card series ended in two-game sweeps, the matchup between the Atlanta Braves and Philadelphia Phillies has delivered exceptional postseason drama. In game one, the Braves trailed late while trying to mount a comeback against typically dominant closer Jhoan Duran. With two outs in the bottom of the 8th down 3-2, third baseman Austin Riley delivered, launching a game-changing homer to give Atlanta a 5-3 lead. articles.title: In 1985, Cristiano Ronaldo was raised in a modest Madeira household with three siblings; years later, he was building a $30M palace overlooking Portugal's Atlantic coast
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo was born in 1985 in Funchal, the youngest of four children in a small Madeira home where space was always short.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo was born in 1985 in Funchal, the youngest of four children in a small Madeira home where space was always short. Decades later, he spent more than three years building a mansion in Cascais, Portugal, with Atlantic views, eight bedrooms and an underground garage for his cars. Reported costs ran from about $30 million to €35 million. Then, just weeks after it was finished, reports said he put it up for sale. The reason had little to do with money. It was privacy.What was Cristiano Ronaldo's childhood in Madeira really like?Ronaldo was born on 5 February 1985 and grew up in Santo António, a working-class neighbourhood on the hillside above Funchal. He was the youngest of four, with older siblings Elma, Hugo and Katia. Money was never loose. His father, José Dinis Aveiro, worked as a kit man at the local club Andorinha. His mother, Maria Dolores dos Santos Aveiro, cooked and cleaned for other families.The family home was small and crowded, and Ronaldo has spoken about sharing a room with his siblings. Privacy was a luxury nobody in that house could afford. Keep that detail in mind, because it matters later in this story.Football filled the gaps. He kicked a ball in the street, at school and around Andorinha, where his father looked after the kit. Even his name came from outside the game. His parents chose Ronaldo because his father admired the actor Ronald Reagan.How did a boy from Funchal end up at Sporting at 12?Talent moved faster than the family budget. Ronaldo played for Andorinha, then Nacional, another Madeira club, before Sporting CP signed him at 12. That meant leaving the island for Lisbon, roughly 1,000 kilometres away, and living in the club's academy.It was not easy. Teammates teased his island accent, and he has talked about the loneliness of those early years. At 15, doctors found a racing heart condition, and he had a laser procedure to correct it. Accounts of that period say he was back training within days.Manchester United signed him in 2003, when he was 18. His father, who had struggled with ill health, died in 2005. From there came the titles, the records and the income that made a project like Cascais possible. The gap is the real story. A boy who shared a crowded home on Madeira ended up with the means to build one of the most expensive houses in Portugal.How much did Cristiano Ronaldo's Cascais mansion actually cost?The house sits in Quinta da Marinha, a prestigious coastal area of Cascais. It is about 30 minutes from Lisbon, and the plot measures 12,000 square metres. Reports describe eight bedrooms, an infinity pool with Atlantic views and a garage built for a car collection valued around €14 million. Earlier descriptions also mentioned glass facades, a cinema room, a gym and a tennis court.The price kept moving. Spanish reports in 2024 put the value near €22 million. Later coverage said the bill reached about €35 million after more than three years of construction. A $30 million figure also circulated, from a Robb Report profile of his property portfolio.Treat every number here as a reported estimate. Ronaldo has not published the real cost. Neighbours also grumbled about the long build, according to Spanish media.Why did Ronaldo put a brand-new mansion up for sale?Soon after the house was ready, Spanish outlet Marca reported that Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez wanted out. The cause was privacy. Ronaldo reportedly tried to buy nearby plots to create distance, but the owners said no. Other outlets then reported a listing at €35 million, matching the build cost.The house was meant to be the family's base after football. Ronaldo plays for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia and was expected to settle in Cascais after retiring. That plan now looks different.A caution is needed. As far as I could find, Ronaldo has not spoken about it publicly. Outlets also disagree on where things stand. One reported the house as sold, while a property guide still lists it as for sale. Treat the privacy explanation as reported, not confirmed.Why does the Cascais story feel so personal for Ronaldo?Consider the contrast. The boy from Santo António grew up with almost no private space. The man built a 12,000 square metre estate and still could not control who could see into it. Money bought land, glass and marble. It could not buy a neighbour's signature.Madeira, meanwhile, never left his story. The island's airport carries his name, a CR7 museum opened in Funchal in 2013, and he keeps a home there. Cascais was meant to be the mainland chapter, close to Lisbon.Property reports also list a Lisbon penthouse and homes in Madrid, Dubai and Saudi Arabia. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Kumkum Mohod, Dhiraj Bommadevara win mixed recurve team silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara signed off with a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event after China’s Jingyi Zhu and Mengqi Li
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara signed off with a silver medal in the mixed team recurve event after China’s Jingyi Zhu and Mengqi Li prevailed 5-3 in a closely fought gold-medal match at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya on Friday.The Indian pair had to settle for silver after fighting back from a 0-4 deficit and briefly threatening to take the contest into a deciding shoot-off. Their medal was India’s sixth in archery at the Games, taking the discipline’s tally to four gold, one silver and one bronze.China made the stronger start, with Dhiraj opening with an 8 before Kumkum followed with a 7. India managed 34 points in the opening set, while Zhu and Li combined for 38 to take the first two match points.India then found itself in a deeper hole in the second set. Kumkum and Dhiraj could manage only 35, while China posted 37 to win the set and move 4-0 ahead.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleIndia fight back from 0-4 downWith China needing just one more set to claim gold, India produced a determined response.Kumkum opened the third set with an 8 but responded with a crucial 10 on her second attempt. Dhiraj helped India post 37, while China finished on 36. Li's final arrow was a 7, leaving the door open for India.The result gave India the set, crucially, they remained alive in the match at 2-4.Kumkum and Dhiraj then produced one of their best shots of the final in the fourth set. Kumkum began with a 9 and Dhiraj followed with another 9 to give India 18 points from the opening two arrows.Kumkum then delivered a 10 before Dhiraj added a 9, taking India to 37. China, however, held its nerve and Zhu and Li matched India's score, with a 10 on their final arrow levelling the set at 37-37.That was enough for China to secure the one point required for gold, leaving India with the silver.Dramatic semifinal comeback against JapanKumkum and Dhiraj had earlier produced a superb comeback to defeat Japan's Nanami Asakuno and Junya Nakanishi 5-3 in the semifinal.India trailed 0-2 after losing the opening set 37-38. The second set ended 36-36, leaving Japan 3-1 ahead, but the Indian pair responded strongly under pressure.They shot 39 in the third set to Japan's 35 and levelled the contest at 3-3. The fourth set then went down to the final arrow, with Nakanishi shooting a 7 to finish on 35. India posted 37 to take the set and complete a 5-3 victory.The silver added to what has been a highly productive archery campaign for India in Aichi-Nagoya.Earlier on Friday, India's women's recurve team scripted a landmark triumph by defeating 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 to win the country's maiden Asian Games gold in the event.Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum held their nerve in difficult windy conditions to overcome the defending champions. India had also defeated China 5-1 in the semifinal.The women's recurve gold was India's fourth archery gold of the Games, following victories in the men's compound, women's compound and mixed compound team events.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Season's over: Caitlin Clark leaves it all on court with bloody mouth as Fever fall in Game 3
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark scored 18 points but the Indiana Fever fell 94-83 to A'ja Wilson's 36-point explosion in a decisive Game 3 elimination in Las Vegas.
articles.body: It was win-or-go-home for Caitlin Clark, and she went down swinging. The season came to an end for Clark and the Indiana Fever with a 94-83 loss to A'ja Wilson and the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces in Thursday's decisive Game 3. Wilson led the charge with 36 points in the winning effort, dropping 21 by halftime. The Fever kept it within single digits until the final two minutes, but the shots just didn't fall down the stretch. Clark — the AP Comeback Player of the Year — finished with 18 points on 6-of-18 shooting. Still, Indiana fought hard to save their season against the reigning champs, headlined by Clark's raw grit. Down 82-77 in the fourth quarter with 3:16 remaining, Clark took a sharp elbow to the face from Jewell Loyd. With her mouth bleeding profusely, she quickly ran back onto the court, fiercely fighting back against head coach Stephanie White and game officials just to stay on the floor. League Double Standards & The Vegas Drama Drama was at a fever pitch coming into Thursday's decisive game in Vegas. A'ja Wilson's technical foul in Game 2 was the talk of the town, largely overshadowing Caitlin Clark's historic postseason milestones. CAITLIN CLARK'S TECHNICAL FOUL SPARKS FURIOUS RALLY AS FEVER AVOID ELIMINATION AGAINST ACES Aces coach Becky Hammon was asked about the Wilson aftermath, which saw her step over and beyond the sideline to confront a fan in the stands. Though clear arguments were made for a suspension, the WNBA made a business decision, looking the other way to leave Wilson untouched by the incident. Speaking on Thursday, Hammon doubled down on her support for her superstar: WNBA REVEALS WHY A'JA WILSON WAS NOT EJECTED FOR APPROACHING FEVER FAN DURING PLAYOFF GAME "I think you saw A'ja get pushed and shoved and there was no response. So there just comes a certain point where a lot of variables come into the exchange that happened the other night. "I stand 10 toes down with the character of A'ja Wilson. And it's like if someone said, 'hey, your brother went and did something.' Like, no, I know the person in the situation, so I trust that person in any situation. And she'll be great tonight. I have no doubt." Fever Coaching Collapse & Off-Court Noise The biggest loser in all of this? Fever head coach Stephanie White. In her second season back in Indiana, White proved she's just a corporate stooge when things get ugly. While opponents treated Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham like punching bags, White hid behind spineless PR fluff instead of defending her stars. In a league that constantly ignores dirty play against its top draw, White refused to go to bat for her team, showing a complete lack of backbone when her players needed a fighter on the bench. FEVER COACH STEPHANIE WHITE LAUNCHES FIERY DEFENSE OF HERSELF AFTER SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM HIT Despite the coaching headaches, the Fever roster still had enough talent to finish 28-16 as the sixth seed. articles.title: Could Commanders get defensive captain back in Week 4 vs Colts?
articles.summary: Could the Commanders get Frankie Luvu back on Sunday?
articles.body:
Will the Washington Commanders get back linebacker Frankie Luvu for Sunday's Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts ? Luvu, who injured his groin in Week 1 at Philadelphia, traveled with the team to London, which was seen as a positive sign that he was close to returning.

Through two days of practice this week, Luvu has participated, but on a limited basis. During Thursday's practice, Luvu didn't look like a player who was limited. He moved around well and showed no signs of a groin injury.

The Commanders need Luvu back. The starting inside linebacker and the player who wears the green dot, Luvu, looked comfortable in Washington's new defensive scheme in Week 1. With Luvu out for the past two weeks, rookie Sonny Styles and Leo Chenal started at inside linebacker. The three were expected to rotate throughout the season. With Luvu out, Styles wore the green dot. Unfortunately, Chenal suffered a neck injury in Sunday's win over Seattle and is out for the remainder of the season.

Luvu was outstanding in his first season for the Commanders in 2024, earning second-team All-Pro honors. However, he struggled last season and often played out of position. Under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, he has returned to what he does best: attacking downhill and occasionally blitzing.

With one practice to go, Washington will likely announce Luvu's status on Friday. The Commanders and Colts kick off at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday in London.

articles.title: Rangers’ Emotional Home Opener Provides Stark Contrast To Last Season
articles.summary: An onslaught of goals, an exuberant crowd, and an incredible goal from Igor Shesterkin topped off the New York Rangers' 5-1 home-opening win over the Tampa B...
articles.body:
An onslaught of goals, an exuberant crowd, and an incredible goal from Igor Shesterkin topped off the New York Rangers ' 5-1 home-opening win over the Tampa Bay Lightning, a game filled with emotion.

Emotions come in different ways, both for the worst and for the better. In the Rangers' case, that is especially true.

Just under a year ago, on October 7, 2025, the Rangers opened up the 2025-26 season at Madison Square Garden against the Pittsburgh Penguins, filled with hope and excitement, as the Mike Sullivan era was set to officially begin.

However, the Blueshirts were shutout, losing 3-0, and they were booed off the ice by their fans in what was a demoralizing way to start a season that would only go downhill from there.

The Rangers' emotions carried from that opening-night game, with the team failing to score a goal over their first three home games, and playing at The World's Most Famous arena became somewhat of a kryptonite for the Rangers throughout much of the season.

Going into Thursday night's home opener, the Rangers were hoping to flip the script from last season and get off to a stronger start in front of their fans, and that's exactly what they did.

Less than 10 minutes into the contest, Mika Zibanejad scored a power play-goal that erased any doubt of another dreaded home scoreless drought ensuing.

"When you can score a goal in the home-opener against a really good team, it gives us a boost of confidence as a group," Sullivan said. "That was a huge goal in the game. Huge part of the game. So much of the game is about momentum, the highs and lows, the ebbs and flows of the emotional rollercoaster ride. When you score the first goal in the way that they scored it, it gives our team juice. It helps us gain momentum. We can build on it, and I thought the guys did a great job after that."

From that point on, the Rangers played off their emotions and continued to build momentum.

The Rangers' offensive dominance continued, adding goals from Pavel Dorofeyev, Eeli Tolvanen, and Gabe Perreault, while they played a noticeably quicker brand of hockey, complimented by a strong forecheck

From a defensive standpoint, the Rangers' penalty kill which featured Noah Laba, Will Cuylle, Tye Kartye, Joe Veleno, Mika Zibanejad, Tolvanen, Sean Durzi, Marcus Pettersson, Vladislav Gavrikov, and Braden Schneider, was able to successfully kill off all seven of the Lightning's power plays, serving as a bright spot for New York.

"This is a whole new team," Sullivan emphasized. "We've got a new group of players, and we're excited about the opportunity we have in front of us. I know how much it means to these guys to win at home. They love playing here. We have such a passionate fan base, and it means a lot to our guys to perform well. I was happy for them.

"I thought it was a solid team effort, top to bottom. We utilized the whole bench throughout the course of the game. The penalty kill was terrific against a real good power play. I just thought it was a great effort to a man."

The high emotions of the night reached a climax when Igor Shesterkin scored a goal in the final minutes of the third period, making history as the first goalie in Rangers history to score.

Shesterkin revealed after the game that this was the first time he scored a goal since he was 19 years old, playing in a junior league.

The moment was truly captured as Shesterkin was swarmed by his teammates after the goal and led the handshake line to the bench with the fans roaring in excitement.

"Well, he made history... You could see the raw emotion on the players on the bench," Sullivan said of Shesterkin's goal. "He's such a great goalie. He makes so many timely saves for us. When he has a moment like that, I think the guys get pretty fired up."

In the grand scheme of an 84-game season, this win is just one small step in what will be a long marathon of a season, but for this team specifically, this victory means a lot more than just two points in the standings.

The past can't be erased, and what transpired during the 2025-26 campaign and specifically the Rangers' play on home ice, was emotionally draining for the entire team.

Still feeling the burden from last season, Sullivan believes the Blueshirts "played with the necessary emotion" but did not allow it to get the best of them.

"We all remember last year," J.T. Miller said. "Like, I'd be lying to you if (I said) we couldn't. But I think we owed it to our fans, and to ourselves, to get rewarded finally, especially to start the season. And we don't have that lingering on us moving forward at home, which is nice. We just played a great game. Really nothing pretty about it.

"I thought that we just made it very hard to play against. You have to against players of that caliber. And when you give them that many power plays, it's tough. But I thought everybody contributed today. Everybody had a commitment to 200-foot hockey. I think that that's what we showed all through camp, and it was nice to put it to work."

Emotions work in mysterious ways. Emotions can be a team's most daunting weakness, as it was for the Rangers last season, or it can be a team's greatest strength, as it was for the Rangers on Thursday night.

Now, they will look to seize this newfound momentum with the hopes of moving forward from last year's failures and starting a fresh chapter.

articles.title: Humphries races into World Grand Prix last eight
articles.summary: Luke Humphries makes it through to the World Grand Prix quarter-finals, along with James Wade, Gian van Veen and Niels Zonneveld.
articles.body:
Luke Humphries has made it through to the World Grand Prix quarter-finals, along with James Wade, Gian van Veen and Niels Zonneveld.

World number two Humphries, who won the tournament in 2023 and was beaten by the eliminated Luke Littler in last year's final, was a comfortable 3-0 winner against Jermaine Wattimena in Leicester.

The Englishman, who hit three 180s and had a highest checkout of 129, will play the Netherlands' Zonneveld, who beat Gary Anderson 3-1, in the last eight.

"It wasn't the best performance, but it was a good performance," Humphries told Sky Sports.

"I think I got in every time with my first three [darts]. When you are doing stuff like that, it is going to take a top performance to beat you.

"I've got a good chance of winning this. At the moment I am a bit up and down, but if I can put that right I am going to be tough to beat."

Wade has won the World Grand Prix twice - in 2007 and 2010 - and kept his hopes of a third title intact with a 3-1 win against Stephen Bunting.

In a tournament where you have to start and finish each leg with a double, Wade took the first two sets and, despite losing the next, won the fourth to secure victory.

Van Veen, who was beaten by Littler in the PDC World Championship final in January and could become world number two unless Humphries wins the title, won the first set against Ryan Searle but then found himself 2-1 down.

He recovered to level before taking the decider to set up a quarter-final against Wade.

articles.title: Hurricanes host Capitals—Preview, How to Watch, Game Thread
articles.summary: Now the grind begins
articles.body:
In a weird way it feels like the season actually begins tonight.

You almost want to write off the first game as with all of the ceremony around it plus the fact that it was the only game in the league for the first two periods. Honestly with the way both teams played you'd be forgiven if you just want to move on from it. Raising the banner and seeing the Storm Surge with the Cup at center ice was great, but that's now all done and there are still 83 games left.

If you're Washington, it's 84 as tonight starts their season. Many thought they would be starting their post-Ovechkin era, but instead he starts his 22nd year with the team on a year-by-year basis. They spent this offseason trying to give him a better year than last.

While Washington made the playoffs by winning the Metropolitan Division in 2025, they missed them entirely in 2026. With Ovi back, the Capitals tried to bolster the team up and down the lineup by acquiring Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou via trades and signing Boone Jenner and Vincent Desharnais. That's a lot of new firepower and their contracts will surely keep them in DC long past the time Ovechkin leaves.

Still, as Tom Gulitti noted in that post, with the condensed preseason and training camp that leaves a lot less time for players to get acclimated to their new linemates and positions. However, they have a solid coach in Spencer Carbery who got a nice contract extension this summer . It also helps they are playing in a division that, on the surface, looks like it may be more forgiving than the Atlantic.

Fortunately Carolina won't have to wait until the morning skate to know the starter, as Washington is starting the season on a back-to-back road trip, so Carbery had to go ahead and prep for who was going to start both games. Tonight, it'll be Logan Thompson . Since he's been in Washington, the Canes are 1-1-1 against Thompson , including going 1-0-1 against him last season as both meetings were before the end of 2025. He only surrendered a total of three goals during those two games, and only gave up one in the shootout. It was a logical choice.

As for the lines, barring a change at morning skate here's what they're starting with.

On Carolina's side, we'll see how Rod Brind'Amour wants to use last change to line up the matchups. Practice on Thursday had the same lines and pairings as we saw on Tuesday night, and it seems pointed that Deslauriers is still going to be out there with Tom Wilson skating around. It's doubful that line would match up with them, but it's more of an insurance policy against someone who likes to throw his weight around.

Pyotr Kochetkov manned the starter's crease on Thursday, but Brind'Amour wouldn't necessarily commit to the starter. Carolina also has a back-to-back, and they'll be hopping a plane to Philadelphia as soon as as this game is done. That's worth noting because, typically, Brind'Amour doesn't like doing a morning skate on a back-to-back so it's possible he would view this as the only chance to get PK some action in that crease before starting him Saturday instead of Friday. That said, we should know after morning skate today who'll man the crease tonight and who'll take on Philly tomorrow.

The other part to know here—tonight is the debut of the Hurricanes Hockey Network for fans inside the Hurricanes broadcast footprint. As a quick reminder—the NHL is the one leading the negotiations for carriage of this and the other three teams (Columbus, St. Louis, and Minnesota) that are utilizing the NHL Central Production unit. As of this writing they have been able to come to an agreement with Spectrum Cable and Fubo if you prefer to get your cable networks through a streaming provider. If you don't have either, you can subscribe to the HHN through Prime Video for $19.99/month or $99/year. The league will continue to negotiate with other providers and supposedly their satellite carrier is set to be announced soon.

That said, if you aren't sure you want to subscribe or you just outright forget before the puck drop, you're likely still going to be able to watch it in North and South Carolina thanks to agreements with WRAL in Raleigh, as well as Cox and Gray Media throughout the Carolinas. This will be a simulcast of the HHN, and together these entities will provide simulcasts of ten Hurricanes games, the other nine being on Saturdays.

As usual if you live outside the footprint, you'll need to have access to ESPN Select (used to be ESPN+, part of ESPN Ultimate and dear God can they just stop with all these names). You can also subscribe to NHL Center Ice if your preference is to avoid ESPN at all costs.

It's always a fun one when the Caps are in town, if you aren't going to be in Lenovo tonight, here's how to catch the action:

TV: Hurricanes Hockey Network. New name, same faces as Hanna Yates and Shane Willis handle the pregame duties at 6:30, and then Mike Maniscalco handles play-by-play with Tripp Tracy providing color. This is also one of the ten "Saturday Night Hockey" broadcasts. Tonight you'll be able to see the simulcast of the HHN on WRAL (Raleigh), WAXN TV64 (Charlotte), WECT 6.1 and 6.2 (Wilmington), WITN 7.1 (Greenville/New Bern), WHNS 21.2 (Greenville SC, Spartanburg SC, Asheville NC), WMBF 32.1 + 32.2 (Myrtle Beach SC), WCSC 5.1 + 5.3 (Charleston SC), and WIS 10.1 + WPAM 18.1 (Columbia SC).

Streaming Video: Hurricanes Hockey Network on Prime Video in the Hurricanes Footprint. Outside you'll need to use the ESPN app and have at least an ESPN Select subscription, which comes with ESPN Ultimate.

Radio: The pregame Storm Watch with Adam Gold on 99.9 The Fan starts at 6:30 PM, At 7 PM the Hurricanes Radio Network (consisting of 99.9, 730 The Game in Charlotte, ESPN New Bern 107.5/1490, and ESPN Greenville 107.5/1570) will pick up the Mike Maniscalco and Tripp Tracy HHN simulcast.

articles.title: Panthers’ Aleksander Barkov goes down with concerning leg injury during Sharks game
articles.summary: Last season, the Florida Panthers dealt with a long list of injuries to key players, many of whom missed significant portions of the campaign. One of their e...
articles.body:
Last season, the Florida Panthers dealt with a long list of injuries to key players, many of whom missed significant portions of the campaign. One of their earliest major setbacks came when captain Aleksander Barkov tore his ACL and MCL during training camp, forcing him to miss the entire 2025-26 season.

Now, there are concerns that Barkov may have suffered another serious leg injury just two games into the 2026-27 season. During Thursday evening's game against the San Jose Sharks, the Panthers captain went down awkwardly in the corner, with his left leg bending awkwardly in the process. He immediately left the ice as a trainer rushed toward the tunnel leading to the locker room to assist him.

Barkov was visibly frustrated as he threw his gloves down while heading down the tunnel toward the locker room.

The Panthers took Barkov in the first round (second overall pick) in the 2013 NHL Draft, and he quickly developed into one of the NHL's premier two-way centers. The longtime Panthers captain has won the Selke Trophy three times as the NHL's best defensive forward, and has become a franchise cornerstone, eventually leading Florida to consecutive Stanley Cup championships in 2024 and 2025. He also helped them reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2023, though they fell short against Vegas.

Barkov has spent his entire NHL career with the Panthers, setting numerous franchise records along the way. He's become one of the most decorated players in team history, and his two Stanley Cup titles made him the first Finnish-born captain to hoist the trophy.

articles.title: Paul Maurice: No Real Update on Sasha Barkov Injury
articles.summary: Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice did not have much of an update on the injury to captain Sasha Barkov, saying […]
articles.body:
Florida Panthers coach Paul Maurice did not have much of an update on the injury to captain Sasha Barkov, saying only that he would get looked at on Friday.

The Panthers will be in southern California as their season-opening road trip continues.

"We'll have a good idea by tomorrow afternoon,'' Maurice said.

On Thursday night in San Jose, Barkov was fighting for the puck in the corner with Darnell Nurse and Zach Ostapchuk when his left leg buckled.

When Barkov hopped off the ice, he pushed open the door on the ice and limped down the tunnel into the visitors' room at SAP Center.

He did not return to the game, one Florida rallied from a 3-0 deficit before losing 4-3 in overtime .

Maurice noted that Barkov's injury on Thursday was not related to the one he sustained to his right knee last September.

Barkov missed all of the 2025-26 season after his right knee buckled in one of his first on-ice drills of training camp.

After having reconstructive surgery on his MCL and ACL, Barkov started skating in January and practicing with the Panthers before the season came to a close.

Although Barkov did not play for the Panthers last season, he would have been cleared had the team made the playoffs.

Instead, he captained Finland to a gold medal at the IIHF World Championship.

Barkov played in his first NHL game since Game 6 of the 2025 Stanley Cup Final on Tuesday against the Carolina Hurricanes.

"It was great, just a little different,'' Barkov said afterward . "The speed of the game is really fast. I missed a whole season, and coming here for the first one, I knew it would be a fast-paced game. I think we did a good job, and I am happy with that.

"I feel good, haven't had any problems with overthinking or anything like that. Just trying to play my game, trying to do my things. I am playing with really good players, and that helps me a lot.''

articles.title: Max Verstappen's Sepang answer has F1 fans falling for him all over again
articles.summary: Asked how he'd prepared for Sepang's heat, Verstappen gave a blunt, funny answer
articles.body:
Press conferences in Formula 1 can come with plenty of rehearsed answers - we all saw Yuki Tsunoda's briefing sheet when he temporarily took Liam Lawson's seat a month ago. These filters can sometimes tame what could be an exciting answer, but it's safe to say Max Verstappen has no such filter as one of his answers on Thursday at Sepang won over fans.

F1 has returned to the legendary track for the first time in almost a decade with it hosting the Bahrain Grand Prix after the original race was cancelled earlier this season. Bahrain keeps the naming rights, but the heat and humidity are very much Sepang's problem now.

And Sepang in October is hot enough for a heat hazard to be declared over the race weekend with air temperatures expected to push past 31C with humidity thick enough to chew on - with a slight chance of rain to keep things exciting.

Max's not-so-serious answer to a serious question

All drivers will prepare in some way for hotter conditions. Some will spend time in similar conditions to adapt their bodies, while others will focus more on hydration or rely on the cooling vest now available to them during sessions. The Dutchman seemingly does very little to adjust.

When asked about this, he answered with a laugh:

"I think I had four or five months of very intense preparation. Yeah, deep mental preparation of not giving an F…!

"Yeah, just rock up. It's hot, but it's also hot in Monaco and it gets very humid there as well and if you really want it hot, you go into the sauna or a steam room. I do that sometimes. You just need to get comfortable with the uncomfortable, but that's the case for everyone. It's hot, sweaty and you need a few more underwears, I guess! But just go with the flow."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes

There was no talk of high temp training or worry, just a guy pointing out that Monaco, where he lives, gets plenty hot enough for him to not need to acclimatise too much for this weekend of racing.

"He's the most relatable guy on the grid and just seems like a regular dude you can grab a beer with. Never change Max," one fan said on a Reddit post on the quote. "I try to channel some Max at work some days," another added.

Don't mistake this for a driver that doesn't care. Verstappen is deeply passionate about his racing and performance, but he's built up a level of callous since his F1 debut in 2015.

"Maximum Max. Any day, any time, any circuit. Life is good," another commented. "I know we like to say Max doesn't care but he very clearly does," added another as a reply read: "I don't always agree with Max on track, but my god he nails off track."

Verstappen finished his press conference admitting he wants at least one win before the season ends while conceding that the Mercedes is the fastest car on most circuits. Regardless of his performance this season, it looks like fans can't get enough of his nonchalant interview answers.

articles.title: “Sorry” – Rooney apologises to £74m Man Utd star after ‘misjudgement
articles.summary: Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney admits he was wrong to criticise Benjamin Sesko over his recent absence without having the full context.The Slovenian s...
articles.body:
Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney admits he was wrong to criticise Benjamin Sesko over his recent absence without having the full context.

The Slovenian striker has been struggling with a shin injury since the end of the previous campaign. After missing the entire pre-season, he made his return off the bench on the opening day of the season in Hull.

However, the 23-year-old's displays were, for the most part, underwhelming. On the final weekend before the international break, Michael Carrick opted to drop Sesko from the matchday squad against Fulham.

Wayne Rooney apologises to Man Utd striker Benjamin Sesko

The big centre-forward's absence at Craven Cottage drew criticism from several pundits and former Man Utd players.

Nicky Butt and Paul Scholes suggested that as long as Sesko didn't have a broken shin, he should have toughened up and taken the pitch.

Rooney was a little less blunt in his assessment, but he did suggest that the player could have taken an injection, as they used to back in the day, and made himself available.

However, it later turned out that Sesko's condition is more serious than initially assumed, and he could be facing another long spell on the sidelines.

Therefore, Rooney felt he had wronged the Slovenian attacker, thus immediately offering an apology for his previous words.

"Well, if it's long-term, then I suppose I should apologise," said the legendary striker in his latest appearance on Stick to United (via RoundTable )

"So, I apologise, Sesko. I apologise if I misjudged you. Sorry."

Michael Carrick given a real dilemma in Sesko's absence

Kudos to Rooney for realising his mistake and making amends, unlike most other pundits who would have escaped the situation.

Nevertheless, the real issue for Man Utd is the absence of a genuine centre-forward at Carrick's disposal.

Joshua Zirkzee is the other recognised striker in the squad, but the Dutchman hardly serves as a focal point in the box, as he prefers to roam all over the pitch, so Carrick doesn't consider him suitable for his system.

The head coach has been relying on Matheus Cunha upfront, but the latter is more comfortable in a supporting role. The same goes for Bryan Mbeumo, albeit he might be a more convincing option than the Brazilian given his electric pace and physical strength.

United's best hope at this stage is for Sesko to avoid a long-term stoppage and make his return to action in the coming weeks.

articles.title: British champion Ursu targets world title shot
articles.summary: Unbeaten British welterweight champion Constantin Ursu says he wants a world title shot within the next 12 months.
articles.body:
Unbeaten British welterweight champion Constantin Ursu says he wants a world title shot within the next 12 months.

The 26-year-old, who is also the Commonwealth champion, retained his belts in August with an eighth-round technical knockout win over Ben Vaughan.

The Moldova-born fighter, who has been based in Plymouth since he was 18, won his Lonsdale belt in March with a points victory over Owen Cooper.

"I want to be world champion next year," Ursu told BBC South West.

"I've been offered two IBO world titles to fight with Jack Rafferty, and they say no," added Ursu, who has won all 16 of his professional bouts.

"But if they change their mind I'm ready to get this fight."

Ursu does not have a bout lined up for the second defence of his British title.

He is keen to ensure he defends his Lonsdale belt twice more so he can keep it for posterity.

But, whoever his next opponent is, he says they will have to be ready for an improved performance from his fight in late August, when he felt he only showed "20% to 30%" of what he is capable of.

"I feel I didn't get my dopamine for my last fight," he said.

"I felt like I didn't go for what I needed to in this fight, I'm not really happy with my last performance.

"So good luck to another opponent because I will give everything for the next fight.

"But it's definitely not my best performance, it's not even close to 50%, 60% of what I have in me."

articles.title: Ibrahim deserves chance to impress - Cleverley

But with Bakinson unable to play against parent club Leyton Orient on Saturday Cleverley says Ibrahim could get his chance.

"He's been brilliant, he's had great impact in the games he's come on, he played well against Palace and his training levels have been really high," Cleverley said.

Este nuevo duelo amistoso servirá a ambos técnicos como laboratorio de pruebas en medio de la preparación para sus próximos desafíos oficiales.

articles.title: Cleveland Browns survive fightback to beat Pittsburgh Steelers
articles.summary: Andre Szmyt landed a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Cleveland Browns a nervy 27-24 win over divisional rivals the Pittsburgh Steele...
articles.body:
Andre Szmyt landed a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Cleveland Browns a nervy 27-24 win over divisional rivals the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Aaron Rodgers had steered the Steelers back from 21-7 down to level inside the last two minutes, but was unable to produce a last-ditch response to Szmyt's winning kick.

Rodgers found Roman Wilson from 12 yards to open the scoring after a lengthy opening drive, but the Browns responded with three unanswered touchdowns in the second quarter.

Chris Boswell ended the half with a 31-yard field goal to cut the gap to 21-10, which remained until Rodgers, who had endured a frustrating evening, cut the gap with a 21-yard scoring pass to Darnell Washington in the fourth quarter.

Szmyt stretched the gap with three points from 44 yards, but Rodgers rounded off a late drive by finding Pat Freiermuth and running in a two-point conversion to level the scores.

But Szmyt struck the decisive blow to lift the Browns to 3-1.

articles.title: Fever eliminated by Aces as Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Mitchell falter
articles.summary: Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark carried the Fever far this season, but the ride came to an end on Thursday.
articles.body:
The Fever went as far as Kelsey Mitchell and Caitlin Clark took them this season. Considering they had arguably the greatest season any backcourt has had in league history, a lot of times, that was pretty far.

But with a chance to exorcise some demons on Thursday, the pair ran out of gas.

For the second straight season, Indiana's season ended in a do-or-die game in Las Vegas as the Aces came away with a 94-83 win. It was a night where Mitchell and Clark combined for 41 points, but shot just 13-41 from the field and 6-23 from three.

"I thought our offense got a little more stagnant in the second half," Clark said. "I felt like we took a lot more late shot clock contested shots where that was our only choice at that point of trying to get something up. You got to give credit to the Aces. I thought they played well. I thought they were ready to go and that's what championship teams do. They played great.

"Like I said, they made it difficult, but we've made a lot of those shots throughout the year too."

The pair came out of the gates clicking in the first quarter, helping Indiana to an early eight-point lead on the road. Through the opening 8:10 of the game, Clark had 11 points and Mitchell seven as Indiana led by four.

But from there, the pair made just six more shots over the final 32 minutes. Clark shot 2-12 from the field, missed all seven of her threes and turned the ball over five times. Mitchell scored eight points in the fourth quarter as the Fever closed to within two points, but still shot only 4-18 from the field in that aforementioned stretch.

"Some of it is we missed some shots," head coach Stephanie White said of the offensive struggles. "We missed some shots that we typically make. There was a level of physicality that we couldn't get to the rim. They turned it up a little bit…It's a game in the margins."

With their backcourt struggling, Indiana turned to both a familiar and an unexpected face to stay in the game. Aliyah Boston finished her strong offensive series with 19 points and 10 rebounds despite being notably hampered.

Myisha Hines-Allen provided a spark off the bench with 12 points and 12 rebounds, her second impactful outing in a row. Her biggest stretch came in the second quarter when the Fever tied the game and forced a timeout after a string of layups.

But no other Fever player had more than five points. And on a night when A'ja Wilson again was in MVP form, Indiana was scratching and clawing just to stay within arms reach of the Aces for most of the night.

The solutions, though, never came offensively. Indiana shot just 6-20 from the field in the fourth, including 3-11 from three. After the Big 3 and Hines-Allen, no other Fever player had more than five points.

The end result was hoping one of Clark and Mitchell could catch fire to save the season down the stretch, but neither could find their groove as the season ticked away.

"I mean, shooters shoot," White said when asked if she considered pulling back the reins on her backcourt. "I think the only thing that we really talk about as the coaching staff is how we get high-quality shots. I mean, look, they're both tough shot makers. They really are tough shot makers.

"How do we get them high-quality shots? How do we get them some easier looks when it starts to go dry a little bit? But there's never a thought, like every time they shoot the ball, I think it's going in, so there's never a thought of anything other than the next one's going in…They made it tough on us and that's what championship teams do."

It leaves the Fever flying back across the country after a season-ending win in the desert for the second straight season. As with most playoff exits, it leaves a bittersweet taste in their mouths — as well as likely a little blood for Clark, too, after taking a shot to the mouth in the fourth quarter — after such a special regular season.

"Just proud of this group," Clark said. "We've weathered a lot. There's always so much outside noise and a microscope on how we perform every day. A lot of really good moments. A lot of tough moments where we probably felt like we gave opportunities away. It's probably what hurts a little bit.

"There was a lot of really good wins and not many nights where me and Kels are going to combine to shoot as poor as we did tonight. That's sometimes a tough pill to swallow. But like I said, still a lot of things to be proud of."
